content:
Sara: FYI Nightjar-40B public beta goes live tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Partner integration may push full traffic. Need a quick infra sanity check for eu-west and us-west.
Dinesh: Copy. Do we have expected RPS and average generated tokens per request?
Lucy: Partner estimates 700-1,100 RPS first hour. Chatty prompts — ~320-500 tokens generated per response. Using upper bound 1,100 * 500 => 550k tokens/sec global if everything hits at once.
James: Is that global peak or per-region? We should split by region for provisioning.
Sara: Global. Anticipated split: eu-west 62%, us-west 28%, asia fallback 10%. So eu-west ~341k tps, us-west ~154k tps.
Dinesh: Quick throughput estimate: Nightjar-40B on A100-80Fp16 with our runtime gives ~180 tokens/s per GPU baseline under steady batching. Streaming & small batches reduce that. Use a conservative 140 tokens/s per GPU for low-latency cases.
Lucy: Do math in thread so it's visible:

```
peak_rps = 1100
avg_tokens = 500
tokens_s = peak_rps * avg_tokens  # 550000
eu_frac = 0.62
eu_tokens_s = tokens_s * eu_frac   # ~341000
gpu_tokens_s = 140
eu_gpus_raw = math.ceil(eu_tokens_s / gpu_tokens_s)
# => ~2436 GPUs (conservative, no batching gains)
```
Maria: That raw number assumes no step-level batching or KV cache reuse. In practice our runtime batching and short contexts give anywhere from 3x-7x tokens/GPU depending on latency tolerance. For a quick planning factor, choose 3.5x.
Dinesh: With 3.5x improvement => eu_gpus ~696. But runtime will see variable batch sizes during streaming. I recommend planning for a low-latency scenario at only 2x improvement => ~1218 GPUs as safety.
Sara: Proposed pragmatic runway (first 6h):
- Reserve eu-west: 800 A100-80 (reserved burst pool)
- Reserve us-west: 400 A100-80
- Cold pool and spot autoscale for additional 40% capacity
- Autoscaler policy: target p50 latency 700ms, p95 1.3s; scale up if p95 > 1.3s for 3m
- Fallback: route overflow to Nightjar-13B-quant at gradual weights if latency breach > 4%
James: Cost note: If we hold 1200 GPUs reserved for 6h at $6/hr => 1200*6*6 = $43,200. Using reserved for EU headroom + spot for burst is cheaper. Finance needs estimate and fast approval.
Finance: Can sign off on up to $35k immediate burn for pre-approved partner launches. Anything above requires exec signoff.
Lucy: Suggest hybrid: reserve EU 800, pre-warm 300 spot nodes with rapid replacement logic, and rely on autoscaler for the rest. Also enable quick model-variant fallback to 13B quant to shed load gracefully.
Maria: Network constraint: eu-west peering to partner uses a single transit; current egress at 82% during peak. If partner ramps instantly, we risk packet drops and TCP stalls. Peering refresh is scheduled next week and cannot be moved without exception.
Dinesh: Ops actions: can we enforce partner-side linear ramp 10m? Or we push a token-bucket throttle in the edge to smooth the burst. @Sara please confirm ramp window.
Sara: Asked partner for a 10-minute linear ramp and got tentative ack. I'll lock it before EOD.
James: I'll set up a quick dashboard (tokens/s, active GPUs, avg batch size, egress Mbps, cost burn rate). Alerts: GPUs >85% for 7m, egress >90% for 5m, cost >1.8x forecast for 15m.
Lucy: Running a simulated stress test tonight at 02:00 UTC that mimics 340k tps in eu-west. Will run 30m and post results + host metrics. If NIC or CPU becomes the limiter we'll add SR-IOV or more 100G links.
Dinesh: Runtime tuning checklist prelaunch:
- ensure KV cache reuse enabled for multi-turn sessions
- enable dynamic batching window to 8ms
- increase max batch size to 256 for background workers
- enable prefetching of embeddings for rerank flows
James: Runbook snippet for rollout:

```
# ramp plan
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood/api/rollouts -d '{"model":"nightjar-40b","weight":0.05}'
# after 10m
# scale group prep
kubectl apply -f nj40b-euw-reserved.yaml
```
Maria: Who owns post-launch cost monitoring and post-mortem if burn exceeds forecast?
James: I'll own the dashboard and first 24h monitoring. If cost > forecast threshold, Finance and GTM will be looped in.
Dinesh: Ops approval ask: eng-infra requests provisional authority to spin up +200 reserved GPUs in eu-west for up to 8h if batching falls below 2.2x effective improvement. Requires finance provisional approval.
Finance: Provisional approval granted up to additional $10k in reserved spend; anything beyond requires exec.
Ops-Bot: Reminder: peering refresh scheduled for 2025-06-02 02:00 UTC. Change freeze exceptions required to move earlier.
Sara: OK plan: partner to ramp 10m, we reserve 800 EU, 400 US, prewarm spots, autoscale with 40% headroom, fallback to 13B quant. Lucy run the load test tonight and paste logs. James build dashboard in next 90m. Dinesh coordinate reserved spin-up automation.
Lucy: Load test scheduled 02:00 UTC. Will post TL;DR + perf counters. Key things I'll check: avg batch size, p95 token latency, NIC drops, GPU % busy.
James: Dashboard ETA 75 minutes, will prewire alerts and slack hooks.
Sara: Thanks team. If partner can't ramp or peering saturates we invoke graceful fallback and slow-roll. Closing thread unless blockers appear. :thumbsup:
